flags.reason: The Amount Input guide and its evidence were checked on 22 September 2026 on jfs-components 0.1.60 (its Sources note still says so); the installed package is 0.1.78 (mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02). Read against the installed AmountInput.tsx, MoneyValue.tsx and NoteInput.tsx, with their tokens through the package's resolver, every sentence this entry quotes still holds, but two NoteInput sentences are out of date. The Sources note's “The NoteInput state prop is accepted but unused by the implementation; its visible editing state is focus-driven.” is contradicted: NoteInput reads state, and state Editing hides the placeholder as focus does (NoteInput.tsx lines 50, 68–69, 170 and 177). The States description's “NoteInput responds to focus and controlled text; its internal state is runtime-driven.” says less than the package: a note with no value keeps what people type on its own and still calls onChangeText (NoteInput.tsx lines 55–57 and 148–151), as the NoteInput guide now says. Both changed between the 8 October (v0.1.78-636f3f5) and 12 October (v0.1.78-c1fa197) builds; AmountInput.tsx itself is the same blob from v0.1.78 to dbe0e02. The entry doesn't quote either sentence. Re-check the guide on 0.1.78 and publish it, then re-extract. Added by Claude Code in the overnight run agentpack-batch13, for Marcin to confirm. Guide fix #536.

dismissed.reason: misreads-source: The anatomy section only says "The component passes its context to both children so their tokens resolve together." The added claim that modes set on the slotted MoneyValue or NoteInput "are replaced by AmountInput's own" describes runtime override behaviour that nothing cited supports.

dismissed.why: The item follows the installed package, not the anatomy sentence alone, which the reviewer sees only as rendered copy. In 0.1.78-dbe0e02, AmountInput.tsx line 37 merges the provider's modes with AmountInput's own, and lines 54–57 and 66–69 return React.cloneElement(slot, { modes }) for each slot element; cloneElement replaces the element's modes prop with that set, so modes set on the MoneyValue or NoteInput in a slot never reach them. AmountInput.tsx is the same blob (3d7ccc3) from v0.1.78 to dbe0e02. The guide's own code sets AMOUNT_MODES on the AmountInput as well as on its children (src/AmountInputGuide.tsx at 31f1c5e, lines 21, 50 and 79–81), so its pages render the same either way.

dismissed.reason: misreads-source: The cited fact only says the resolver falls back to the collection's default mode (Default). The 'renders smaller' observation in the evidence is about Storybook's default story, which "relies on ambient context". That is not shown to be Context3=Default, so the general claim that an unset Context3 renders smaller than 56 px / 32 px goes beyond the evidence.

dismissed.why: The item rests on the package, not on the Storybook observation. The facts give Context3's default as Default (the resolver uses it when modes leave Context3 unset), and AmountInput sets no Context3 of its own (AmountInput.tsx lines 36–37 merge only the provider's modes and its own). Through the package's getVariableByName on 0.1.78-dbe0e02, moneyValue/value/fontSize and moneyValue/currency/fontSize, which MoneyValue.tsx reads (lines 174–178), resolve to 14 px and 14 px with no modes or with Context3 Default, and to 56 px and 32 px with Context3 Amount Input. So an AmountInput with no Context3 set, by its own modes or a provider, renders the amount and currency smaller than the Amount Input entry; the rule makes no claim about ambient context.
